sections.h2: No city transfer tax in Crystal Lake
sections.html:
Crystal Lake charges no city transfer tax, and the McHenry County Recorder confirms that no municipality in the county charges its own. The state tax still applies.

The city sits about 45 miles northwest of Chicago and is the county's most populous city. Population is 42,288, up 5.0 percent from the 2020 count of 40,269. About 77.6 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, with a middle value of $311,400, and households earn a middle income of $108,418. The city has 14,806 households of about 2.72 people. This is an owner market with steady demand, so a house in good shape has real options beyond a cash sale.

sections.h2: The sale process step by step
sections.html:
A Crystal Lake sale follows the standard Illinois sequence, with only a few city-level touchpoints. You sign a contract, deliver the disclosure report, clear title, pay off any mortgage, sign the deed and have it recorded with the McHenry County Recorder.

Offices that touch a Crystal Lake home sale
OfficeWhat it handlesPhone
City of Crystal Lake, Water BillingStarting or ending water and sewer service(815) 459-2020
City Building DivisionBuilding, electrical and plumbing permits; code enforcement(815) 356-3605
McHenry County RecorderRecords the deed and holds the declaration filed with it815-334-4110
McHenry County TreasurerQuestions on property sold for back taxes815-334-4072
McHenry County AssessorOwner and parcel information815-334-4290

A new deed is required to change ownership, and the Recorder suggests using an attorney. Deed forms are free at the office. The PTAX-203 or MyDec form filed with the deed shows the full consideration, which is the base for the state tax of fifty cents per $500 in Article 31 of the Property Tax Code.

Before you sign anything, gather your latest tax bill, your mortgage payoff figure, the permits you pulled and any warranty papers. At the closing table you sign the deed and the declaration, the title company pays off your lender and prorates the taxes, and the deed goes to the Recorder. Call Water Billing a few days ahead so the final reading lands on the closing date. With a cash buyer the same steps apply, but the appraisal and lender underwriting drop out, which is where most of the time savings come from.

sections.h2: City rules for sellers and buyers
sections.html:
Crystal Lake's rules are mostly about utilities, permits and streets. There is no point-of-sale inspection. City Hall stands at 100 W. Woodstock Street, with weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM and a main line of (815) 459-2020.

  • Permits: the Building Division issues building, electrical and plumbing permits and enforces the building, housing, pollution control and fire codes. If you started a project and did not finish it, call before you list.
  • Water and sewer: the buyer sets up service by contacting Water Billing, and the city offers a Direct Debit Program.
  • Garbage: the city's residential contractor is Lakeshore Recycling Systems, which provides weekly curbside collection and one bulk item per week.
  • Street parking: parking on city streets is prohibited from 2:00 AM to 6:00 AM year-round, which matters for open house guests.

Open permits and unfinished work tend to surface in inspection and title review, so closing them out before listing avoids a later argument.

Buyers sort Crystal Lake by neighborhood and school boundary more than by city name. Downtown surrounds Crystal Lake Central High School and has the widest range of house sizes and ages. Directly south is the Coventry neighborhood, and southwest of downtown is the sprawling Four Colonies area. South of that are The Villages, named for Village Road.

North of downtown, the area near Prairie Ridge High School has large houses on widely spaced lots, and Burtons Bridge sits at the northeast edge next to the Fox River.

Outdoor recreation helps listings. The separate Crystal Lake Park District runs more than 40 parks, including 140-acre Veteran Acres Park and 305-acre Lippold Park.

Crystal Lake buyers frequently commute, so schools and the Metra station are the first questions. Community High School District 155 runs the high schools, and Crystal Lake Community Consolidated School District 47 operates the elementary and middle schools. Part of the northeast side is served by Prairie Grove Consolidated School District 46.

The Metra Union Pacific Northwest Line runs to Chicago's Ogilvie Transportation Center, with stops at Crystal Lake and Pingree Road. U.S. Route 14, Illinois Route 176 and Illinois Route 31 serve the city by road, and O'Hare International Airport is about a 45-minute drive. Mention the train and the district in your listing or when you talk to a buyer, since both shape what a family will pay.

sections.h2: What an Illinois seller must disclose
sections.html:
Illinois law has the seller fill in a residential disclosure report and hand it over ahead of signing. The duty is in Section 20 of the disclosure Act, and Section 35 holds the form.

The report covers flood hazard insurance, flooding or recurring leakage in the basement or crawl space, whether the property is in a floodplain, and defects in the foundation, roof, walls, electrical, plumbing and heating systems. It also asks about wells, septic and sanitary sewer systems, radon, asbestos, lead, mine subsidence, termites, underground fuel tanks and boundary disputes. The form requires an explanation for any answer of yes or not applicable, except on the first question.

Answers rest on what you actually know, with no special investigation required. The form is a disclosure rather than a warranty and leaves room for a buyer's own inspection.

Condition, deadline and appetite for effort decide it. Cash makes sense for a house needing repairs, a firm move-out date or a wish to skip showings, and a listing suits a house that is ready to show.

  • List the repairs a buyer's inspector would flag and get bids for them.
  • Add the cost of carrying the home while it is listed, including taxes, utilities and insurance.
  • Ask what closing date the buyer will commit to in writing.
  • Confirm any open permits are closed or that the buyer accepts them.

Tax bill information is on the McHenry County Treasurer's site. Ask the title company to show the prorated tax lines on your settlement statement, and keep your latest bill handy.

If the house is not ready to show, ask a cash buyer to put the offer in writing with the closing date, who pays title and recording charges, and what happens if the inspection turns up something new. Then set that figure next to the net from a listing after repairs, carrying costs and commission. The better choice is the one that leaves more in your pocket by the date you need to move.

faqs.q: Does Crystal Lake charge a transfer tax when I sell?
faqs.a: No city tax exists, and the McHenry County Recorder confirms that no municipality in the county levies one. The state tax still applies.

faqs.q: Is a city inspection required before a Crystal Lake sale?
faqs.a: No point-of-sale inspection is required. Call the Building Division at (815) 356-3605 to ask about open permits on the property.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded for a Crystal Lake property?
faqs.a: It is recorded with the McHenry County Recorder. A new deed is required to change ownership, and an attorney is recommended.

faqs.q: How do I end water service when I sell?
faqs.a: Contact the city's Water Billing office at (815) 459-2020. Ask about the final reading and how the closing date will be handled.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Crystal Lake house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the Illinois disclosure report reaches the buyer first. The form itself recognizes that parties may agree to an as-is deal.
